name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.dek: Microsoft Windows. Confirmed exploited in the wild. Federal remediation due 16 October.

items.title: Zod 4.6.6 compromised by malware?
items.dek: Zod npm package 4.6.6 hit by supply-chain malware; evidence of active compromise in transit dependency.
items.unproven: scope and exploit chain of malware payload not detailed; no confirmation of how many installs received infected version

items.title: Show HN: Parsimony – an open-source benchmark for how much code AI models add
items.dek: Parsimony benchmark measures coding units added by AI models across existing SWE-bench patches; informs model selection when integrating code generation into SDLC.
items.unproven: whether metric predicts long-term maintenance burden in production codebases or correlates with security debt

items.title: (Post-Quantum) Cryptographic Right Answers
items.dek: Filippo Valsorda post-quantum cryptography guidance; taxonomy and naming conventions for key rotation.
items.unproven: specific to Valsorda's recommendation set; does not evaluate competing frameworks or organizational readiness

items.title: I Found a $90k Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google
items.dek: $90k Google RCE writeup; single finding disclosed post-remediation, not actionable threat.
items.unproven: vulnerability already patched; demonstrates no ongoing exposure to reader's environment

items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
items.dek: Anthropic describes its internal source control architecture; applicable insights are organizational and tooling patterns, not technique.
items.unproven: generalization beyond Anthropic's scale and deployment model; transferability to financial services SDLC unclear.

items.title: Crypto thieves sell hardware wallets with secret eSIM
items.dek: Supply-chain attack on hardware wallets via compromised eSIM; threat to end users, not developers.
items.unproven: this is a supply compromise, not a software vulnerability; outside the reader's remit
